data.name: Tutorial_P0_Body
data.value:
RemEx 2.0 turns your PC into a secure remote command center. Monitor hardware sensors, launch apps, manage files and processes, and stream your desktop from your phone or a second desktop client.
Your PC runs RemEx Host, and every connection is protected with TLS plus PIN-based pairing.

data.name: Tutorial_P1_Body1
data.value: This desktop app includes an embedded RemEx Host that starts automatically. Your Android phone connects to it — not the other way around.

data.name: Tutorial_P1_Body2
data.value: For always-on access (even when you're not logged in), you can install the host as a Windows service or Linux daemon. This lets your phone connect anytime.

data.name: Tutorial_P2_Body1
data.value: To keep RemEx running 24/7 without being logged in, install it as a Windows service:

data.name: Tutorial_P2_Steps
data.value: 1. Open Settings (⚙) → scroll to 'Windows Service' 2. Set your Windows username and password 3. Click 'Install as Service' 4. The service starts automatically on boot

data.name: Tutorial_P2_Note
data.value: The service runs under your user account so it can access your desktop session for screen capture and app launching.

data.name: Tutorial_P3_Body1
data.value: On Linux, RemEx Host installs as a user-level systemd service so it can start with your session and stay available in the background.

data.name: Tutorial_P3_Steps
data.value: 1. Download the latest Linux host archive from GitHub Releases. 2. Extract it. 3. Run ./install.sh install inside the remex-host folder. 4. Use systemctl --user status remex-host to verify it is running.

data.name: Tutorial_P3_Link
data.value: Tip: use the bundled install.sh script instead of copying service files by hand.

data.name: Tutorial_P4_Body1
data.value: For detailed hardware monitoring (300+ sensors), install HWiNFO64 — it's free for personal use.

data.name: Tutorial_P4_Steps
data.value: 1. Download from hwinfo.com 2. Run HWInfo → Settings (⚙) → Main Settings 3. Check 'Shared Memory Support' → OK 4. HWInfo must be running for RemEx to read its sensors

data.name: Tutorial_P4_Warning
data.value: ⚠ HWInfo's Shared Memory auto-disables after 12 hours (free version). Re-enable it periodically, or consider the Pro license.

data.name: Tutorial_P5_HWInfo
data.value: 🟢 HWInfo: 300+ sensors — CPU temps, GPU clocks, fan speeds, voltages, power draw. Requires HWInfo running.

data.name: Tutorial_P5_BuiltIn
data.value: 🪟 Built-in: Basic sensors — CPU usage, RAM, disk I/O, network rates. Always available, no extra software.

data.name: Tutorial_P5_Body2
data.value: Pin your favorite sensors to the Home screen from Settings → Pinned Sensors.

data.name: Tutorial_P6_Body1
data.value: The App Launcher lets you start programs on your PC from your phone. Apps must be configured here first.

data.name: Tutorial_P6_Steps
data.value: 1. Navigate to the Launcher page (sidebar) 2. Click '+ Add Program' 3. Browse to the .exe or shortcut 4. Launch from your Android app!

data.name: Tutorial_P6_Note
data.value: This works even with the standalone Remex.Host service — configure apps in the desktop client at least once.

data.name: Tutorial_P7_Body1
data.value: Your Android app finds this PC automatically using mDNS. Both devices must be on the same Wi-Fi / LAN.

data.name: Tutorial_P7_Body2
data.value: If auto-discovery doesn't work, find your PC's IP manually:

data.name: Tutorial_P7_IpSteps
data.value: Windows: CMD → ipconfig → 'IPv4 Address' Linux: ip addr or hostname -I

data.name: Tutorial_P7_Body3
data.value: Then enter the IP address and port in the Android app. If this device is not paired yet, enter the 6-digit PIN shown on the host.

data.name: Tutorial_P8_QR_Body1
data.value: The fastest way to connect your phone is by scanning a QR code. The host generates a pairing code that contains everything your mobile app needs.

data.name: Tutorial_P8_QR_Steps
data.value: 1. Open Settings → Connection on the host 2. Click "Show QR Code" 3. Open the RemEx mobile app 4. Tap the QR scanner icon on the connection screen 5. Point your camera at the code — you'll connect automatically!

data.name: Tutorial_P8_QR_Body2
data.value: No typing, no IP addresses — just scan and go. The connection details are saved so you only need to scan once.

data.name: Tutorial_P9_Body1
data.value: File Transfer only shows the folders your PC host has shared. Configure them from Settings on the desktop host so your phone sees the right locations.

data.name: Tutorial_P9_Steps
data.value: 1. Open Settings → Shared Folders on the PC host. 2. Keep RemEx Transfers writable for quick phone → PC uploads. 3. Leave other folders read-only unless you want mobile devices to modify them.

data.name: Tutorial_P9_Body2
data.value: On your phone, browse a shared folder, tap a file to download it, or upload from Android into any writable folder.

data.name: Faq_Q1_Question
data.value: What do I need to run on my PC?

data.name: Faq_Q1_Answer
data.value: You need either RemEx Desktop Client or RemEx Host running on your PC. The desktop client bundles the host automatically; the standalone host is ideal for background-only installs. Download the latest package from GitHub Releases, install it, and keep it running before pairing.

data.name: Faq_Q2_Question
data.value: How do I pair my phone or second PC?

data.name: Faq_Q2_Answer
data.value: Use Settings → Connection on the desktop client to show a QR code or pairing PIN. Scan the QR code from Android for the fastest setup, or enter the 6-digit PIN manually when the app prompts for secure pairing.

data.name: Faq_Q3_Question
data.value: How do I find my PC's IP address?

data.name: Faq_Q3_Answer
data.value: Windows: 'ipconfig' in Command Prompt. macOS: System Settings -> Network. Linux: 'ip addr' in terminal. You can also see the IP directly in the Remex.Client.Desktop window.

data.name: Faq_Q4_Question
data.value: Auto-discovery isn't finding my PC. What should I check?

data.name: Faq_Q4_Answer
data.value:
1. Make sure RemEx Desktop Client or RemEx Host is running.
2. Both devices must be on the same Wi-Fi / LAN.
3. On Android 13+, allow Nearby Wi-Fi Devices; on Android 17+, allow Local Network access too.
4. Check whether your router has AP/Client Isolation enabled.
5. Corporate or guest networks often block mDNS discovery.

data.name: Faq_Q5_Answer
data.value: The default port is 5005. If port 5005 is in use, it will fall back to 5006. You can see the active port in the desktop client's window.

data.name: Faq_Q6_Question
data.value: Can I connect over the internet?

data.name: Faq_Q6_Answer
data.value: RemEx is designed for local network (LAN) use. You can use a VPN for remote access. Port forwarding is not recommended for security reasons.

data.name: Faq_Q7_Question
data.value: Remote Desktop is laggy. What can I do?

data.name: Faq_Q7_Answer
data.value:
• Lower the Quality slider.
• Reduce Target FPS (15-20 is usually enough).
• Lower the Scale.
• Verify your host supports DXGI (Windows) or X11/Wayland capture (Linux).
• Prefer a fast local 5 GHz Wi-Fi network.

data.name: Faq_Q8_Answer
data.value: Wake-on-LAN lets you power on your PC remotely. Enable it in your BIOS/UEFI and network adapter properties. Then enter your PC's MAC address in the Connection screen.

data.name: Faq_Q9_Answer
data.value: Open File Transfer from the sidebar or command palette. You'll only see the folders the host has shared, and writable roots accept uploads while read-only roots stay download-only.

data.name: Faq_Q10_Question
data.value: Can I lock my PC remotely?

data.name: Faq_Q10_Answer
data.value: Yes. Use the Remote Control screen or command palette on desktop, or add the Lock PC Quick Settings tile on Android for one-tap access.
